newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico 755 MW unit restarting, 187 MW unit out.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico 755 MW unit restarting, 187 MW unit out.

text.p: Output at the 755 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Four Corners, N.M., coal-fired power plant was up to 70 MW after being shut late Saturday due to a fan problem, sources familiar with the unit said early Thursday.
"Barring any more problems -- and keep in mind that we had four different things to fix -- we should be at full load around (1300 MST)," said one source.
Meanwhile, the 187 MW unit 2 at the Four Corners plant was said to be shut because of a tube leak.
An estimate for its restart was not immediately available.
Four Corners' 750 MW unit 5, 186 MW unit 1 and 244 MW unit 3 were said to be operating normally.
Arizona Public Service, which operates Four Corners, owns units 1, 2, and 3 along with 15 percent of units 4 and 5.
Southern California Edison Co holds a 48 percent stake in units 4 and 5.
